extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: Common Corpus is the largest open dataset for LLM pre-training, containing approximately 2 trillion tokens of data that are either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses. It is multilingual, covering a wide variety of languages from major European languages to low-resource ones, and includes code data, government documents, scientific texts, and web content across diverse domains and time periods.
extraction.license: Public Domain, CC-BY, MIT, CC-BY-SA, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, BSD-2-Clause, CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0
extraction.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov (PleIAs)
extraction.inLanguage: en, fr, de, es, la, it, pl, el, pt, ru
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Common Corpus was assembled by aggregating data from multiple open sources including digitized cultural heritage collections (books, newspapers), government and legal documents, scientific publications, open-source code, and web content. Data was collected from national libraries, government agencies, international organizations, and open data portals. The collection process involved downloading entire dumps, API access, and reuse of pre-existing datasets. Data was filtered for copyright compliance (public domain or permissive licenses), post-processed for OCR correction, toxicity filtering, and PII removal.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes digitized books and newspapers from national libraries (e.g., French National Library/Gallica, Library of Congress, German Digital Library, National Library of New Zealand), government and legal documents (SEC filings, USPTO patents, EUR-lex, court records), scientific publications (OpenAlex, ArXiv), open-source code, and web content. Sources span multiple languages and time periods from the 17th century to the present.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data collection began in May 2023; the current version was released in February 2025. Source documents span from 1618 (Europeana Newspapers) to 2024 (SEC filings), with some sources covering as early as 1690 (US PD Newspapers).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has uneven language coverage, with low-resource languages being underrepresented. The dataset is also skewed toward European languages and historical texts.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Common Corpus does not cover the full range of available open data (open data paradox), has shallow coverage for low-resource languages, is limited in size for training very large models, does not contain instruction-tuning data, and curation methods cannot guarantee 100% accuracy (e.g., residual OCR errors, potential PII, toxicity).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Common Corpus enables open LLM research and development while complying with copyright and AI legislation, reducing legal uncertainty and supporting open science. It also demonstrates that LLM development is possible under strict regulatory norms, including EU AI regulations.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset underwent PII removal as part of curation, indicating that personal information may have been present in source data. Toxicity detection was also applied.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for pre-training Large Language Models. It is not directly suitable for instruction-tuning or task-specific fine-tuning, but it opens opportunities for creating ethical fine-tuning datasets due to its multilingual, temporal, and semantic diversity.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus is an ongoing effort with plans to expand coverage, particularly for European languages (as part of the LLMs4EU project) and African languages. The dataset is available on Hugging Face.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Post-processing and filtering of Open Culture data; OCR correction using OCRonos model; toxicity filtering; removal of personally identifiable information; text segmentation using Segmentext model; OCR error detection using OCRoscope and OCRerrcr tools
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtering by publication date (retaining only titles published prior to 1884 for public domain verification); rights verification pipeline including author life + 70 years rule, publication + 95 years for US authors, and Wikidata-based data reconciliation; OCR processing using Nautilus-OCR for some datasets; language detection using cld2; text segmentation; OCR error detection and correction

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce Common Corpus, the largest open dataset for language model pre-training.

description.evidence: The data assembled in Common Corpus are either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses and amount to about two trillion tokens. The dataset contains a wide variety of languages, ranging from the main European languages to low-resource ones rarely present in pre-training datasets; in addition, it includes a large portion of code data.

creator.evidence: Pierre-Carl Langlais Carlos Rosas Hinostroza Mattia Nee Catherine Amett Pavel Chizhov Eliot Krzystof Jones Irène Girard David Mach Anastasia Stasenko Ivan P. Yamshchikov PleIAs, Paris, France

datePublished.evidence: In this paper, we present Common Corpus, which has been an ongoing effort since 2024

inLanguage.evidence: Token counts for the ten most represented languages in Common Corpus: English, French, German, Spanish, Latin, Italian, Polish, Greek, Portuguese, Russian

isLiveDataset.evidence: Common Corpus, which has been an ongoing effort since 2024... It has grown to become the largest open dataset for pre-training Large Language Models at about 2 trillion tokens

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Large portion of data in Open Culture part of the Common Corpus was built on top of the following collection-as-data initiatives... Gallica: about 85B words of digitized French newspapers and monographs made available on the open data portal of the French digitized library through entire dumps or API access

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Common Corpus was built on top of the following collection-as-data initiatives... The dataset was curated by using the Library of Congress JSON API... It was originally published as part of the Pile of Law

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Common Corpus is composed of six collections: Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Web, Open Code, and Open Semantic... Chronicle America: about 100B words (150B tokens) of digitized US newspapers by the Library of Congress... Gallica: about 85B words of digitized French newspapers and monographs... SEC annual reports (Form 10-K) for the years 1993 to 2024

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: Common Corpus was first conceptualized in May 2023... The current version of Common Corpus, the one we describe in this paper, was released in February 2025 for the Paris AI Summit... The articles were published between the years 1690 and 1963... SEC annual reports (Form 10-K) for the years 1993 to 2024

rai:dataBiases.evidence: even though the language diversity of the data is large, the coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow. We are developing in this direction, planning for enlargement of the corpora in African languages (e.g., Swahili, Wolof, Bambara).

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Common Corpus is far from collecting the whole range of available open data, which we call the open data paradox... the coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow... the amount of collected data (2 trillion tokens) is suitable for pre-training of models of limited size... Common Corpus naturally does not contain data for instruction-tuning and any forms of specialized tasks... none of the curation methods could naturally facilitate a hundred-percent accuracy.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Through the release of Common Corpus and this paper with thorough documentation of data collection and curation, we show that LLM development is possible while strictly adhering to the regulatory norms. We hope that Common Corpus will grow as a critical infrastructure for open science LLM research and development and inspire future initiatives in the open.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: even though we used these methods responsibly and mitigated many issues overlooked by the counterparts (e.g., with toxicity detection and PII removal), none of the curation methods could naturally facilitate a hundred-percent accuracy.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Common Corpus naturally does not contain data for instruction-tuning and any forms of specialized tasks. Therefore, it is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning. However, due to the multilingual, temporal, and semantic diversity of data, Common Corpus opens the opportunities for the creation of ethical fine-tuning datasets.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Continuing the work, we are currently collecting more data in European languages as part of the LLMs4EU project. In addition to this, even though the language diversity of the data is large, the coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow. We are developing in this direction, planning for enlargement of the corpora in African languages.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: The Open Culture data in Common Corpus have been post-processed and filtered... we engage in extensive OCR correction and toxicity filtering in order to bring datasets up to standard... We remove personally identifiable information from our datasets

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: To ensure that these texts are in the public domain, we have retained exclusively titles published prior to 1884... we also implemented an internal data reconciliation pipeline based on the complete dump of Wikidata... OCR was done using Nautilus-OCR... one short n-gram is classified as unknown by cld2
